checks_actual_results: Execution context passed before implementation. The existing flow version, execution, action, history, task and job storage were reused; no duplicate workflow engine, scheduler, backend, frontend or Redis service was added.
The designer exposes a published child-flow selector, inherit switch and separate structured input/output mapping rows with add/remove controls. Users do not enter flow IDs or JSON.
Publication rejected self references, unavailable unpublished children, cross-scope invalid targets, duplicate mapping targets and direct or indirect subflow cycles.
Publication froze the child flow version, definition hash, name and version number. A parent published before child V2 continued to start frozen child V1.

Runtime persisted reciprocal parent-instance, parent-execution, node and child-instance links. Child success applied explicit output mappings and resumed the exact parent execution once under a stable idempotency key.

Child exception remained visible while the parent waited. Child incident could be manually resumed; rejected, terminated or withdrawn children produced a recoverable parent incident instead of silently completing the parent.

Terminating a parent recursively terminated active child chains and cleared their tasks, jobs and active executions. Two same-backend restarts preserved waiting and terminal parent-child relations and did not duplicate parent resume.

Ordinary designer and runtime GUI checks showed structured mapping controls, frozen child version, readable parent-child links, waiting/completion/exception/termination history and translated terminal task states.

Eleven isolated actual case groups covered publication guards, frozen version and mappings, failure visibility, restart recovery, exactly-once resume/replay, incident recovery, cascade termination, ordinary GUI and exact cleanup.

JDK21 Maven package with FlowSubflowPolicyTest passed. The final frontend production build passed with only the pre-existing bundle-size warning. Targeted git diff --check passed with existing CRLF normalization warnings only.
Cleanup disabled owned flows 148-156, left zero unfinished tasks, jobs and executions for owned instances 254-259, and preserved existing Module51.
permission_or_failure_result: Subflow targets and frozen versions are server-authoritative. Publication blocks self/cyclic/unpublished targets and invalid mappings; durable reciprocal links plus SUBFLOW_RESUME:<parentExecution>:<childInstance> prevent duplicate parent continuation; failures remain visible and recoverable, and parent terminal state cannot leave active child work.
remaining: This closes the bounded subflow lifecycle contribution. Remaining automatic business, notification, wait/timer, webhook/external nodes, controlled applications, external channels and all other product requirements remain required.
next_scope: Implement structured automatic business data nodes over the verified common action executor: field update and data create/update choose authorized modules, operations and fields through controls, publish an immutable safe configuration, execute idempotently with permission and version checks, expose readable success/failure/retry history, and verify actual API/database/GUI/replay/restart/cleanup without JSON or raw action codes.
integrated_verification: 11 actual case groups, focused backend package/test, frontend production build, ordinary GUI, API/database readback, two same-backend restarts, idempotent replay and exact cleanup passed.
